title: Latency-Throughput Correlation Probebook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note documents a set of reproducible experiments and an operational checklist to investigate how throughput settings, client pacing, and warmup behavior correlate with tail latency and GPU occupancy. The goal is to build a small, repeatable harness and a set of analysis heuristics we can use whenever a change to runtime batching, kernel selection, or routing policy is suspected of changing the p95/p99 tradeoff for steady throughput.

Why this doc (context):
- We keep seeing runs where nominal throughput is stable but p99 regresses after a kernel change; root cause often hidden in warmup/occupancy drift.
- Existing bench notes focus on priming/warmup best practices; this doc aims to tie those to explicit correlation checks, thermal/occupancy probes, and a short experiment matrix we can run in ~2-3 hours.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Use a two-stage run: deterministic micro-probe (20–40s) to capture latency distribution at low concurrency, then steady-state run (10–30 min) with controlled pacing and seeded RNG.
- Always capture: client-side timestamps, server trace-id, gpu_util, mem_used, pcie_counters (if available), nvlink errors, and kernel timelines.
- Warmup protocol: 6 minute thermal hold + staged concurrency ramp (0% -> 30% -> 60% -> target) with occupancy checks at each step.
- Repeat each config 3 times with different RNG seeds but identical pacing; compare p50/p95/p99 and occupancy variance.

Harness design decisions (notes to self):
- Determinism vs realism: We must balance clients that are synthetic (fixed prompts) and those that mimic token length variance. For correlation probing, start synthetic (fixed 128-token prompts) to reduce variance, then run one realistic workload sweep.
- Two-level measurement: short micro-probes to isolate tail behavior, long runs to observe drift and thermal effects.
- RNG hygiene: seed loadgen client RNG and record seed; keep client-side sequence identical across repeats except seed-driven sampling of samples.

Minimum data capture (must always be collected):
- client.request_ts, client.response_start_ts, client.response_end_ts
- server.request_recv_ts, server.response_send_ts (trace id correlated)
content_addendum:
- GPU metrics sampled at 1s: gpu_util, gpu_mem_used, sm_efficiency (if available), power_draw
- Runtime internal metrics: batch_size_histogram, kv_cache_hits, batching_latency_ms, scheduling_backpressure_ms
- System metrics: cpu_load, irq, network_tx/rx, disk_iops (for on-prem)

Loadgen config snippets (example):
- micro-probe (fast):
  - duration: 30s
  - concurrency: 4
  - prompt_template: fixed-128-tokens.txt
  - seed: 12345
  - pacing: open-loop (no artificial client sleep)
  - expected_output: debug-mode (include token-level timestamps)

- steady-state (long):
  - duration: 1800s (30m)
  - concurrency: target_conc (see matrix)
  - pacing: closed-loop with 10ms jitter (to avoid perfect alignment), max inflight per-client: 2
  - seed: 12345 (and 67890, 24680 for repeats)

Example YAML-style pseudo-config (for the harness):
  name: steady-throughput-probe
  workload: fixed-128
  duration_s: 1800
  concurrency: 64
  pacing: closed-loop
  client_jitter_ms: 10
  rng_seed: ${SEED}
  capture_token_timestamps: true

Warmup sequence (recommendation):
- pre-heat (thermal hold): 6 mins at low concurrency (8–16) with a few heavy synthetic requests to spin up power governors.
- staged ramp: 3 mins at 30% target, 3 mins at 60% target, then go to target. At each stage sample GPU metrics for at least 60s and verify occupancy stdev < 5%.
- sanity micro-probe: 30s at target concurrency; fail-fast if p99 > slow_threshold (configurable per model).

Repeatability checklist (do before every bench):
- [ ] Node pool allocation is stable (no scheduled infra jobs).
- [ ] Run on pinned model revision & image tag, record git sha.
- [ ] Disable autoscaling and any background cold-starts.
- [ ] Set client RNG seed and record it in run metadata.
- [ ] Confirm sampling frequency (1s) for GPU metrics is enabled and consistent.
- [ ] Capture kernel selection logs (env RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel).
- [ ] Note ambient rack temperature for on-prem testbeds.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Axis A: concurrency levels (8, 16, 32, 64, 128)
- Axis B: batching_policy (aggressive | conservative | hybrid)
- Axis C: quantization mode (fp16 | int8-ptq | int8-qat)
- Repeat each cell 3x seeds (seedA, seedB, seedC)
- Metric outputs per cell: throughput (tokens/s), p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), occupancy_mean, occupancy_std, batch_size_mean, kernel_switch_count

Quick commands (example, replace INFLIGHT/SEED/OUTPUT):
- start micro probe: ./bench/run_loadgen --config micro-probe.yaml --seed 12345 --out micro-12345.json
- start steady run: ./bench/run_loadgen --config steady-throughput-probe.yaml --concurrency 64 --seed 12345 --out steady-c64-12345.json
- collect metrics: ./bench/collect_metrics --run steady-c64-12345.json --out metrics-c64-12345.csv
- gcloud/pagerank: Ensure instance labeling: --labels=bench=latency-probe,seed=12345

Analysis heuristics (how to look for correlation):
1) Correlate short micro-probe p99 spikes with kernel_switch_count bumps. If micro-probe shows clean p99 but long run regresses, suspect thermal or occupancy drift.
2) Plot occupancy_mean vs p99 over time (sliding 60s windows). Strong positive correlation indicates batching backpressure or cache thrash.
3) Inspect batch_size_histogram: high mass at small batch size with latency spikes points to scheduling preemption.
4) If GPU util is high but throughput lower than expected, check KV cache hit rate and NVLink/utilization — model fanout could be causing cross-device stalls.

Failure modes we've seen (notes):
- invisible kernel fallback: a kernel selector starts using a slower kernel for some sequence lengths — surface via kernel_switch_count and binary kernel tags in logs.
- warmup insufficient: occupancy drifts upward slowly over 10–20 minutes; long runs show tail growth even when micro-probes pass.
- client alignment: perfectly periodic client pacing produces micro-synchronization and artificial throughput peaks; jitter solves this.

Desired additions and next steps (short backlog):
- Add an automated post-run script that computes correlation coefficient between occupancy_std and p99 and flags runs with r>0.6. (GH PR stub: GH-rl/runtime-bench#142)
- Add thermal sensor export to bench collector for on-prem racks.
- Build a dashboard (Console) tile that overlays batch_size_histogram with p99 heatmap per minute.

Notes to collaborators / open questions:
- Hannah: can you add the kernel selection debug macro to the standard bench image and push an image tag?
- Diego: please confirm which NVLink counters are accessible on the new A100 boards in our testbed.
- Priya: propose slow_threshold values for the family of large models (gpt-like 7B/13B/70B) we use.

Attachments / references (search terms to find related notes):
- search: "occupancy drift" OR "kernel_switch" OR "batch_size_histogram" in serving-runtime drive
- related Confluence: serving-runtime-benchmarks -> calibration and warmup
- related GH: runtime-bench repo under tools/bench

Small TODO (immediate):

-- end --
